Dağıtımda etkinlik: The production of goods and services in line with consumer preferences and demands.
Dealer: The name given to persons and institutions acting in their own name and on their own account in purchase and sale transactions.
Decreasing Returns to Scale: The case where, while all production factors increase at the same rate, the quantity of output increases less than the increase rate of the production factors. Hence the rate of increase in output is smaller compared to the increase in input quantity. In this case, as the quantity produced rises, long-run average cost increases.
Deflasyon: Refers to a continuous fall in the general level of prices.
Deflatör: Refers to the price index used to convert the value of an economic quantity expressed in monetary (nominal) terms (for example wages, raw material prices, costs, etc.) into its real value.
Delivery Pricing: In sectors where transportation costs are significant, if sellers and buyers are dispersed across regions far from one another, final prices can differ substantially. In such sectors, if the product is homogeneous and demand elasticity is low, undertakings seeking agreement on price setting can overcome this problem with 'delivered pricing'. Delta: The first derivative of the option price with respect to the price of the underlying asset (Δ = ∂C/∂S = N(d1)); in Black-Scholes, the delta hedge is constructed with this ratio.
Denge döviz kuru: The exchange rate at which purchase and sale transactions take place when the foreign exchange market is in equilibrium.
Denge faktör bileşeni: The factor bundle used in producer equilibrium.
Denge fiyatı: The price at which transactions take place when the market is in equilibrium.
Denge gelir düzeyi: The total quantity of production realized when the economy is in income equilibrium.
Denge genel fiyat düzeyi: The general price level formed when the economy is in income equilibrium.
Denge miktarı: The quantity of a product bought and sold when the market is in equilibrium.
Denge tüketim paketi: The bundle of products purchased in consumer equilibrium.
Denge ücreti: The wage level formed when the labor market is in equilibrium.
Denk bütçe çarpanı: The coefficient showing how much effect a unit change in government expenditures, made in a way that keeps the budget balanced, will have on equilibrium income.
Depresyon: Or depression (crisis): although there is no precise definition, a severe and prolonged recession affecting multiple countries, in which total output falls by more than 10 percent.
Devalüasyon: Under a fixed exchange rate regime, refers to the decrease in the value of the national currency against foreign currencies. For example, the fall of the value of one Turkish lira against one US dollar from 2.0 TL to 2.2 TL means that the Turkish lira has lost 10% in value against the US dollar (the US dollar has gained value).
Devlet: The central or local governments that influence the economy through the laws they enact and the policies they implement, and that themselves also produce and consume.
Devlet aksaklığı: The view that the state is also made up of people, and that these individuals, whether politicians or bureaucrats, can act in line with their own personal interests.
Devlet harcamaları: The sum of the state's consumption and investment expenditures.
Devlet harcaması çarpanı: The coefficient showing how much effect a unit change in government expenditures will have on equilibrium income.
Devlet iç borçlanma senedi: Or in short DİBS: the bonds and bills released into the domestic market by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance.
Devlet İç Borçlanma Senetleri: Debt securities issued in the domestic market by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance of the Republic of Türkiye.
Devletin tüketim harcamaları: Or in short G: the main expenditure heading covering the purchases of goods and services the state makes domestically in order to fulfill its services.
Devralma: A firm's acquisition of the majority or all of the partnership shares belonging to another firm, thereby obtaining the management of that firm.
Değer kaybı: The decrease in the value of an asset or a currency against other assets or currencies due to market conditions.
Değer kazancı: The increase in the value of an asset or a currency against other assets or currencies due to market conditions.
Değer saklama aracı: The function and property of money enabling the purchasing power currently on hand to be used in the future as well.
Değer çelişkisi: The phenomenon of the price of some goods of vital importance to people being cheap, while the price of some relatively unimportant goods is high.
Değere göre vergi: A tax taken on the monetary value of the object subject to the tax.
Değişim aracı: The function and property of money being used in the purchase of goods and services.
Değişken Faizli İhraçlar: Instruments whose return is linked, without being fixed at issuance, to other variables determined in advance. Issues indexed to realized inflation, or to the past 3-month average of international interest rates such as LIBOR, fall into this type. In environments where uncertainty in return (interest) rates increases and price formation becomes difficult, the risk is lower for both issuers and the individuals and institutions investing.
Değişken faktör: Or a variable input: production factors whose quantity can be changed at any desired time.
Değişken gider: Expenses such as raw material and electricity consumption that vary depending on the quantity produced.
Değişken girdi: Or a variable factor: production factors whose quantity can be changed at any desired time.
Differentiated Products: Products containing real or perceived physical differences or features, on account of which one is preferred over the other, are considered differentiated. Products are differentiated by undertakings with the aim of selling at a higher price and/or increasing sales. Differentiation can be based on physical appearance, quality, durability, tied services (warranties, after-sales services and information), image and geographic location. Dikey birleşme: The merger of two firms relating to different parts or production stages of a certain product or product group.
Diligence (on New Technologies): The diligence due from financial institutions so that new technologies are not used as a tool in money laundering. Accordingly, financial institutions should exercise special care against new and advanced technologies that pose a money laundering danger by concealing identity information, and take the measures necessary to prevent these technologies from being used for money laundering purposes; in particular, they should have policies and procedures identifying the risks for business relations and transactions not carried out face to face
Dip: The point at which economic activity reaches its lowest level at the end of a recession process.
Dirsekli talep eğrisi modeli: Or the Sweezy model: an oligopoly model in which the demand for a firm's good depends on the response of rival firms to a price change.
Discrimination: The act of putting the parties to transactions at a disadvantage in competition by applying unequal rules for equal exchanges. Discrimination by proposing different conditions to buyers in equal positions for equal rights, obligations and performances can be evaluated as one of the forms of abuse of a dominant position.
Divestiture: Refers to practices such as the relevant undertakings separating a certain asset, business or line of business from their structure and transferring it to other undertakings, or the transfer of the shares providing control of an undertaking, in order to remedy the competition problems that arise or may arise.
Divestiture Trustee: The person appointed by the parties with the aim of continuously monitoring, on behalf of the competition authority until the closing of the transaction, whether the commitments accepted in merger or acquisition decisions are being complied with, and of contributing to the implementations. In Turkish practice, this appointment by the parties must be approved by the Board.
Diğer her şey sabit: Or the Latin ceteris paribus: the assumption that all other effects are held constant while examining a certain economic relationship.
DİBS ya da devlet iç borçlanma senedi: The bonds and bills released into the domestic market by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance.
Dolarizasyon: The use by residents of a country of foreign currency instead of their own national currency as a medium of exchange, unit of account and store of value. Full dollarization is a country's completely abandoning its national currency and adopting a foreign currency as its official currency. Partial dollarization arises when economic units in a country, in an environment of high inflation and uncertainty, begin to prefer financial assets in foreign currency instead of financial assets in national currency, in order to protect themselves from the possible loss of value of the national currency. It is generally observed that the first stage of dollarization develops as 'asset substitution', the beginning of the use of foreign-currency assets as a store of value. On the other hand, the banking crises frequently experienced in the recent past, particularly in emerging markets, have added to the economics literature the concept of 'liability dollarization' in addition to asset dollarization. Liability dollarization is the holding of large amounts of foreign-currency liabilities by all economic units in the country, including the banking and public sectors. Both asset and liability dollarization can be gathered under a single heading and characterized as 'financial dollarization'. Financial dollarization is defined as the tendencies of residents of a country to hold both their assets and their liabilities in foreign currency.
Dolaylı kotasyon: Or in short ED: the exchange rate showing how much foreign currency can be bought in exchange for one unit of domestic currency.
Dolaylı müdahale: The practices by which the state influences the market through taxes or incentives.
Dolaylı talep: Or derived demand: the situation where the demand for an object depends on the demand for the good, service or investment instrument produced or acquired by using that object.
